title: Engagement econ metrics playbook + sprintboard
body:
Purpose and audience:
This note is a working sprintboard + concise playbook for Customer Success leads running QBRs with engineering stakeholders. Focus: four canonical operational KPIs we bring to renewal conversations: median latency (p50/p95), service availability (uptime/SLA compliance), effective unit cost (cost/token), and cache efficiency (cache hit rate).

Why a compact playbook?
- CS needs reproducible definitions so metrics shown to customers match what infra/product reports.
- Provide calculation recipes, quick SQL/PromQL snippets, thresholds for health categories, and suggested talking points.
- Include an actions checklist (triage -> RCA -> mitigation -> customer comms) for each metric.

Definitions (single-line canonical forms):
1) Median (p50) and 95th (p95) end-to-end latency: time from request received by our public API gateway to final token emitted (ms).
   - Canonical formula: latency_ms = response_timestamp - request_ingest_timestamp (gateway).
   - Use p50 for steady-state performance signals; p95 for tail behavior customers feel.

2) Uptime / availability (SLA compliance): percentage of 5xx/error-free request minutes over rolling 30d relative to total minutes, weighted by customer tier.
   - Canonical formula: uptime_pct = 1 - (sum(error_minutes) / total_minutes) * 100.
   - Discrete incident windows are counted as minutes with elevated 5xx rate > 1% of requests for that minute.

3) Cost per token (effective): total inference spend (cloud + infra amortized) / billable tokens processed over window.
   - Include: GPU runtime, instance overhead, cross-region egress, quantization licensing if applicable, and cache storage ops when they materially change egress.
   - NOTE: for customer-facing statements show both raw unit cost and normalized (net of discount & reserved capacity amort).

4) Cache hit rate (prefix/KV): fraction of token generation requests served from a cache layer (full or partial) that avoided a full forward pass.
   - Canonical formula: cache_hit_rate = served_from_cache_tokens / total_requested_tokens.
   - Track both prefix-cache and response-cache separately.

Quickcalc examples (for QBR slides):
- If last 30d invoiceable tokens = 1,250,000 and infra spend allocated = $3,125 -> cost/token = $0.0025/token.
- If total requests in window = 120,000 and p95 latency = 620ms, call out tail as: p95(620ms) vs p50(180ms).

PromQL / SQL-ish snippets (examples to hand to infra dashboards):
- p95 latency (PromQL): histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(api_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le))
- Uptime (minute-window): 1 - sum_over_time((rate(errors_total[1m]) > 0.01)[30d:1m]) / (30*24*60)
- Cost per token (SQL-like): SELECT SUM(gpu_cost + instance_cost + egress_cost) / SUM(billable_tokens) FROM infra_billing WHERE date BETWEEN X AND Y;
- Cache hit rate: SUM(cache_served_tokens) / SUM(total_requested_tokens) GROUP BY customer_id

Health thresholds (recommendation):
- Latency:
  - Green: p95 < 350ms and p50 < 120ms
  - Yellow: p95 350-700ms or p50 120-250ms
  - Red: p95 > 700ms or p50 > 250ms
- Uptime:
  - Green: >= 99.95% over 30d
  - Yellow: 99.5% - 99.95%
  - Red: < 99.5%
- Cost per token (business-tier relative):
  - Green: within 10% of expected baseline for tier
  - Yellow: 10-30% deviation (investigate batching, quantization, caching config)
  - Red: >30% deviation (immediate review with infra/product)
- Cache hit rate:
  - Green: >= 30% effective hit for predictable workloads (chat or assistant flows with prefix reuse)
  - Yellow: 10-30%
  - Red: < 10% (likely no effective caching, evaluate prompt engineering + caching policy)

Suggested actions per metric (compact playbook):
- Latency red -> Immediate: open "latency-tail" incident, collect traces, compare model variant routing, check autoscale events. Triage owners: SRE + Serving Runtime + Customer Success TPM.
- Uptime red -> Pager to SRE + Oncall infra; publish incident timeline to CS and schedule postmortem within 72h.
- Cost spike -> Pull per-request token delta, check for policy/regression in batching or quantization. If caused by model change, revert rollout.
- Cache miss surge -> Run prefix reuse audit and review cache eviction / TTL policies; recommend prompt templates to customers to increase hit rate.

RCA checklist (for QBR appendix):
- When flagging a KPI change, attach: time series screenshot, query used, top-5 contributing routes/models, config changes (rollouts, kernels, quantization), and estimated customer impact.

Sample customer-facing KPI table (copyable into QBR slides):
Metric | Definition | 30d target | 30d result | Trend | QBR talking point
--- | --- | ---: | ---: | --- | ---
p95 latency | end-to-end ms | <350ms | 410ms | ↗ | We saw tail pressure during peak 9-11 PST; SRE implemented burst autoscale and we expect p95 to fall next week
p50 latency | end-to-end ms | <120ms | 165ms | ↘ | majority of calls remain fast but tail increased due to longer sequences on model X
Uptime | % availability (30d) | 99.95% | 99.87% | ↘ | Two short incidents accounted for 5 minutes of error time; reviewing regional failover
Cost per token | $/token (net) | $0.0026 | $0.0031 | ↗ | Higher due to increased short-lived requests and fewer cached responses; exploring batching improvements
Cache hit rate | % tokens from cache | 30% | 21% | → | Cache helps but prefix reuse hit domestic traffic more than APAC; suggest template changes for APAC clients

Customer QBR script snippets (one-liners):
- "Our SLA this quarter remained above 99.8%, with two small incidents that we’ve already remediated; remediation steps and estimated timeline is in the appendix."
- "Tail latency increased primarily due to a rollout of model X; we paused that rollout and re-routed traffic to the prior variant while we tune kernel choices."

Operational templates to attach to QBR: (links or copy into slides)
- Incident summary template (1-pager)
- One-line RCA timeline + impact table
- Action tracker with owner + ETA (30 / 60 / 90 days)

Open questions / backlog items (for CS + infra sprint):
- Standardize billing attribution for hybrid cache-by-token events (who gets credited?)
- Build a canned dashboard tile for 30d normalized cost/token that adjusts for reserved capacity amortization
- Add a cache-hit breakdown by prompt-type (system vs user tokens)

Next steps for this doc:
- Convert to a slide deck for the next CS enablement (owner: Aisha) by 2025-03-15
- Run a short playbook dry run with 2 renewal owners (Marisol, Jonah) and capture friction points

Notes to self: keep this lightweight. customers want simple signals, not infra noise. Attach raw query examples and CSV extracts as appendix rather than slide main content.
